newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola up as funds buy old-, new-crop spread.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola up as funds buy old-, new-crop spread.

text.p: WCE nearby canola traded up as funds bought 1,300 July-Nov spreads while bearish USDA soybean estimates earlier Thursday weighed on new crop.

"Funds bought 1,300 July-Nov at $41, commercials are covering shorts, selling deferreds. The USDA soybean number was bearish," a trader said. July WCE futures crush margin rose to -7.50 Thursday from -8.94 Wednesday.
July canola rose $1.10 to $406.80 at 1110 CDT, November down $1 to $366. July flax lost $0.80 to $334.50 on commercial selling, November up $1 to $317.50 on dry weather concerns.
"Weather's in the back of everyone's mind," a trader said.
The Canadian Wheat Board cut Prairie wheat yields by 0.5 bushels an acre on Wednesday due to lack of rain in the southeastern Prairies.
July western barley lost $0.30 to $131.30 as Alberta Wheat Pool liquidated July longs, October up $0.40 to $133.40, a trader said. July-Dec spread at $3. Oats did not trade.
July wheat down $0.70 at $157.30, December up $0.40 to $159.80 as commercials bought on dry weather concerns.
July feed peas lost US$1 to US$183, October fell US$0.90 to US$182 on commercial sales. July-Oct US$1.
(All prices in Canadian dollars/tonne except oats, peas).
